tasks.gr9-rise-of-hitler-t1: Topic: Rise of Hitler and Nazism. Cover the Weimar Republic and its economic crisis after World War I, Hitler's rise to power and Nazi ideology, establishment of a fascist dictatorship in Germany, persecution of minorities especially Jewish people, and Nazi expansion into Austria, Czechoslovakia, and Poland. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain why the Weimar Republic was unstable, identify Nazi policies of control and persecution, sequence Hitler's territorial expansion, analyze causes of Nazi support, and explain how Hitler dismantled democracy.
tasks.gr9-holocaust-genocide-t1: Topic: The Holocaust and Genocide. Cover the systematic persecution and murder of six million Jewish people and millions of others by Nazi Germany, escalation from discrimination to ghettos to extermination camps, the role of the state in organizing genocide, concentration camps and death camps (especially Auschwitz-Birkenau), and the moral imperative to remember and prevent future genocides. Ask Grade 9 learners to define genocide, explain the escalation of persecution, identify major death camps, analyze how states can become instruments of mass murder, and explain why Holocaust remembrance matters.
tasks.gr9-world-war-2-allies-axis-t1: Topic: World War II: Allies and Axis. Cover the main belligerents (Axis: Germany, Italy, Japan; Allies: Britain, Soviet Union, USA), the war in Europe including the fall of France and the Blitz, Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union, the war in the Pacific including Pearl Harbor and island-hopping, and the outcome (German surrender May 1945, Japanese surrender August 1945 after atomic bombings). Ask Grade 9 learners to classify nations as Axis or Allied, sequence major battles, explain why the USA entered the war, analyze the Holocaust's context within the war, and describe the scale and consequences of global warfare.
tasks.gr9-resistance-to-nazism-t1: Topic: Resistance to Nazism. Cover forms of resistance (sabotage, hiding refugees, spreading banned information, armed rebellion), internal opposition including the White Rose student group and military plots, the July 20, 1944 assassination attempt on Hitler led by Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg, resistance movements in occupied Europe (French Resistance, Polish Home Army, partisan fighters), and individuals who risked or lost their lives to oppose evil (Righteous Among Nations). Ask Grade 9 learners to identify forms of resistance, analyze why resistance was dangerous, explain the moral significance of opposing evil under totalitarianism, and discuss whether armed or nonviolent resistance was more effective.
